key_insight: A two-stage Mamba-based sequence model can jointly classify superconducting qubit states and correct relaxation-related readout errors with higher fidelity and far fewer parameters than prior ML readout methods.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster, lighter readout pipeline for frequency-multiplexed superconducting processors, directly improving scalability and lowering logical error rates in quantum error correction workflows.
method: Stage 1: perform initial qubit state discrimination on readout traces.
Stage 2: refine predictions by detecting and mitigating relaxation-induced errors.
Use Mamba sequence modeling for linear-complexity inference on variable-length traces.
evidence_signal: The model achieves geometric mean readout fidelity of 0.906, with an optimal variant at 0.911, while reducing parameter size by 49.6% and maintaining 0.893 fidelity at 500 ns readout durations.
watch_item: Performance is reported on specific superconducting readout traces, so deployment may still require hardware-specific calibration and validation under different noise, crosstalk, and multiplexing conditions.
paper_title: Multi-Stage Mamba-Based Architecture for Fast and Scalable Superconducting Qubit Readout
